recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. If FM wants single Claim.item.serviced[x] instants to carry time-of-day precision, handle that as a new explicit source-changing decision that considers the long publication history and aligned financial resources.
issue_request: FHIR-7314 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification FHIR-core Claim change request from the 2015May ballot asking that Item.serviceDate support procedure time ranges affecting billing; the recorded resolution said to change the data type to a choice of DateTime or Period.
initial_application: No FHIR-7314-keyed source commit was found. December 2015 Claim history changed Claim.item.serviceDate from date to a date|Period choice in commit 649fcd4cbf21557ae6db78e0afb908f3030dad7a, then renamed the element to Claim.item.serviced[x] in commit 6850355e894c42a480ba652b6a8ad1b7e722f477 while preserving date|Period; later source conversions preserved that shape.
additional_context: Claim is active in the current build. Current source/claim/structuredefinition-Claim.xml defines Claim.item.serviced[x] as date or Period, and STU3, R4, R5, and the current build claim.profile.json all expose date|Period. Related FHIR-8958 and FHIR-7315 are already represented on the combined branch by no-change audit commits. No relevant Zulip or Confluence evidence was found.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Claim.item.servicedPeriod already provides dateTime-bounded periods for the billing time-range use case, and changing the long-published date branch to dateTime now would be a separate non-compatible schema decision rather than a safe application of this old tracker.
